title: Marker, Popup and Tile Source Map
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: MicroSims
Maps
Leaflet
Geographic Coordinates
Web Mapping
description: A Leaflet MicroSim of seven Minneapolis museums and parks in which learners switch tile sources, open popups, recolor markers by category and deliberately swap one marker's latitude and longitude to distinguish the separate roles of marker, popup and tile source.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: Markers, popups, tile sources and latitude-first coordinates in Leaflet
learningObjectives: The learner will distinguish the roles of the marker, the popup and the tile source by changing each one independently and observing the result.
prerequisites: Latitude and longitude in decimal degrees
Map marker, popup, tile source and layer control (Chapter 9)

dependencies: Tile servers: OpenStreetMap, OpenTopoMap, Esri World Imagery (network required)

accessibility.notes: Markers are keyboard-focusable with titles and alt text; controls are native checkbox and buttons; the caption is an aria-live region; categories are named in labels, not color only

dataFiles: data.json (seven Minneapolis landmarks with lat, lng, category, description)

controls.label: Base map
controls.purpose: Switch the tile source; the attribution changes with it

controls.label: Marker
controls.purpose: Open the marker's popup and show its category in the info panel

controls.label: Show category
controls.purpose: Recolor pins and labels from the category field

controls.label: Swap lat/lng / Restore lat/lng
controls.purpose: Reverse one marker's coordinates to show latitude-first order

controls.label: Fit all markers
controls.purpose: Zoom to the current marker positions

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Isolate-one-variable exploration with a deliberate error
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Map explorer with independent layer controls
keyQuestions: What does each of the marker, the popup and the tile source contain?
Why does the attribution change when the base map changes?
Where does a marker land if its latitude and longitude are swapped, and why?
commonMisconceptions: Coordinates are written x,y so longitude comes first in Leaflet (Leaflet takes [lat, lng])
The popup is part of the base map (it belongs to one marker)
Attribution is optional decoration (it is a license requirement of the tile source)
assessmentOpportunities: Written list of which layer each change affected
Correct marker code for a new location
